title: How do you read a scatter plot in a case interview?
description: How to read scatter plots quickly, spot the relationship and the outliers, and turn them into a case insight, with a worked store-performance example.
hook: Scatter plots show how two things move together, and the most useful insight is often not the trend but the dots that break it. Here is how to read one fast and say something sharp.
body:
What it shows

Each dot is one item (a store, a product, a country) placed by two measures, one on each axis.

A worked example

Each dot is one of 40 stores: store size on the horizontal axis, profit on the vertical. Most dots rise together: bigger stores earn more. But five large stores sit near zero profit.

Insight: "Size usually predicts profit, but five large stores are clear underperformers. They are the first place to look: what do they have in common? Location, management, competition?"

How to read one in 30 seconds

  1. Read both axes and their units.
  2. Look for the overall pattern: up, down or no relationship.
  3. Find the outliers, the dots far from the pattern.
  4. Ask what explains the outliers, and say what you would check.

Common traps

  • Assuming the pattern means one thing causes the other.
  • Ignoring the outliers, which are often the real story.
  • Not noticing a log scale on an axis.
outro: Next in this topic: How do you read stacked bar charts without missing the real story?
